page: Microsoft Azure D64lds_v5 is a 64-vCPU virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base clock of 2.8 GHz. The underlying topology provides 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, supported by 48 MB of L3 cache, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and hardware acceleration flags including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance allocates 128 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2 GB per vCPU, alongside 2,577 GB of integrated local solid-state storage. No discrete graphics processors or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark data reflects strong multi-threaded compute capabilities alongside high uncached memory throughput. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 61,072.79, a Geekbench multi-core score of 16,454, and a stress-ng multi-core result of 62,160.81. High-throughput operations are further evidenced by large-block memory read bandwidth of 290.71 GB/s, write bandwidth of 133.7 GB/s, and a Redis throughput of 69.1 million SET operations per second. Conversely, single-thread performance benchmarks such as stress-ng single-core (1,899.88) and Geekbench single-core (1,668.0) fall squarely within median tiers, indicating that parallel execution is essential to extract maximum efficiency from the hardware allocation.

With its 2 GB per vCPU density and sizable local NVMe SSD, the configuration emphasizes computational capacity over high per-core memory allowances. This layout represents a cost-efficient resource profile for parallel compute jobs that require rapid scratch storage without the overhead of massive memory footprints. Ideal workloads include large-scale software compilation, distributed caching nodes, batch data transformations, continuous integration pipelines, and high-concurrency static web serving.
